title: P0-C: Figure 4 omission-identity spike provenance -- pipeline verified clean, full-corpus run blocked on a missing metadata sidecar directory (not a code bug)

generated.summary: Read-only audit of the complete Figure 4 evidence chain (NWB -> unit identity -> trial/slot ontology -> spike feature construction -> target labels -> grouping/cycles -> CV -> permutation null -> source table -> panel/stats receipt), per the 2026-08-15 PRGS instructions' P0-C gate list. The pipeline actually wired to the figure (context/figures/fig04_omission_identity_decoding/fig04_safe_renderer.py, fed by scripts/compute_omission_identity_leakage_safe.py) is a SEPARATE, independent implementation from jnwb/omission_identity.py's decode_identity_cycle_deconfound (which feeds scripts/compute_omission_identity_cycle_deconfound_v3.py and was the subject of the P0-A unit-identity fix and the PROJECT_STATE.md 'do not promote 0.601' addendum) -- neither the P0-A nor P0-B fixes touched this code path, and it did not need them: it independently uses row-position unit identity from the start (session.get_units(area).index, self-documented per output row) and its own leave-one-cycle-out CV with a within-cycle-permutation null via the shared jnwb.permutation.permute_labels primitive.

links.reasoning: Same P0 priority list, same class of hazard (unit identity), but this audit found the Figure-4-facing pipeline is a different implementation that was never exposed to that bug.

notes: GATE: p4 label fix -- PASS. OMISSION_IDENTITY_CONDITIONS['p4'] in jnwb/omission_identity.py (lines 38-45) already carries the 2026-08-06 A/B-swap fix, and compute_omission_identity_leakage_safe.py imports this dict directly, so all three slots (p2/p3/p4) it iterates use the corrected labels.

GATE: unit identity unambiguous -- PASS. _spike_count_matrix() (compute_omission_identity_leakage_safe.py:279-297) uses `list(units.index)` (row position) directly; never touched the unit_id column. Each output cell row records unit_identity='session.get_units(area).index row position' as self-documenting provenance.

GATE: grouped/cycle-safe CV -- PASS. assign_temporal_cycles() (gap-based, median-positive-gap x 10 threshold) assigns cycle ids; decode_binary_cycle_safe() and decode_multiclass_cycle_safe() both use leave-one-cycle-out folds with per-fold class-balanced training subsampling.

GATE: adequate permutation count with seed recorded -- PARTIAL/UNVERIFIED AT SCALE. DEFAULT_PERMUTATIONS=1000, DEFAULT_SEED=42, both recorded per-cell and in the run receipt. But the only receipts that exist on disk (outputs/classification/fig04_smoke/ and fig04_smoke3/, both dated 2026-08-10) used n_permutations=5 and n_permutations=10 respectively on 1 and 3 sessions -- neither is the corpus-scale run this gate requires. No 1000-permutation, full-corpus receipt exists.

GATE: intended corpus rerun -- FAIL (not yet done, not a regression). No outputs/classification/omission_identity_leakage_safe_{cells,oof,folds,null}.csv exist at the default path; no context/figures/fig04_omission_identity_decoding/svg/ directory exists. Figure 4 has never actually been rendered from this safe pipeline. This matches PROJECT_STATE.md's existing Figure 4 table row, which already lists this as a requirement, not a completed step -- this audit confirms and specifics that open state rather than discovering a new defect.

GATE: no hardcoded scientific panel -- PASS. fig04_safe_renderer.py's six panels (A-E2) all either raise on missing/incomplete leakage-safe input or compute directly from the loaded CSVs. Panel A is schematic only (task-structure diagram) and is explicitly labeled 'estimator': 'schematic only' in the figure's own provenance receipt schema -- not a hardcoded scientific value.

GATE: spatial/hierarchy model named according to what was actually fitted -- PASS (resolved by pipeline replacement, not by renaming). The REVISION_PLAN.md-flagged 'GLMM mislabel' (omission_identity_glmm_coefficients_v2.csv describing an L2-regularized logistic regression as a GLMM) is not referenced anywhere in the live renderer or producer -- grep confirms it appears only in already-quarantined scripts/historical/confounded/* and historical .lab receipts. The current pipeline's estimator is honestly recorded as sklearn.svm.SVC (linear kernel) in every cell row and the run receipt; no GLMM claim exists on this path.

GATE: null headline accepted if corrected decoding is at chance -- NOT YET APPLICABLE. No corpus-scale result exists yet to accept or reject; this gate cannot be evaluated until the corpus rerun (blocked, see below) completes.

BLOCKER (root-caused, not resolved): the corpus rerun requires session_readiness.csv's sidecar_ok gate, which is False for all 22/22 current sessions because jnwb.paths.meta_dir() (D:/analysis/metadata) does not exist on this machine -- D:/analysis/ exists and has tfr_arrays/ populated (2026-08-12) but no metadata/ subdirectory at all. The only script that ever wrote it, scripts/archive_oneoff/build_session_sidecars.py, hardcodes ITS OWN pre-remap output path (D:/workspace/data/metadata/{stem}/) in its docstring -- the exact layout jnwb/paths.py (2026-08-08) documents as superseded by D:/analysis/*. This script has not been rerun against the current canonical path since the drive-remap/path-centralization work (commit 39541b8). The 2026-08-10 smoke runs (3/9, 1/9 eligible) predate this and must have used a since-superseded readiness snapshot. This is an infrastructure/data-materialization gap, not a code defect -- flagged per the project stop condition ('a readiness gate reports zero eligible sessions while the artifacts it gates exist on disk') rather than resolved unilaterally.

compute_omission_identity_leakage_safe.py's own readiness filter (_resolve_sessions) requires sidecar_ok even though the script itself only ever reads NWB directly via session.get_units()/get_epochs()/get_spike_times() and never touches the sidecar CSVs -- this may be an inherited/overly-conservative gate rather than a genuine dependency, but that determination and any fix were explicitly deferred to a follow-up cycle by user direction (2026-08-17), not decided here.
